cards.text: Friend, this Gospel opens like a song, and it starts before there was anything at all. "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God." Then the next line: He was with God in the beginning.

cards.question: The Word was with God, and the Word was God. Through the Word, ___ things were made.

cards.text: ALL of it, baker, from every star in the sky down to every dust bunny in the back of my old junk drawer. And then: "In Him was life, and that life was the light of men."
The Light shines in the darkness, friend. And me? I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, so me and darkness are on a first-name basis.

cards.question: The darkness has overcome the Light.

cards.text: Now a man shows up who was sent from God. His name was John, the one we know as John the Baptist (Matthew 3:1), and he came as a witness to testify about the Light.

cards.question: John the Baptist came to testify about the Light. Why?

answers.text: So everyone might believe through him
So people would come to follow him
So the temple leaders would listen

cards.question: John the Baptist was the Light himself.

cards.text: Now the true Light, the one who gives light to everyone, was coming into the world. EVERYONE, friend, even a dusty old stamper from the back of a drawer.
He was in the world, and the world was made through Him.

cards.question: The world was made through the true Light, and now He's in it. What does the world do?

answers.text: It crowns Him as its king
It runs and hides from Him

cards.text: Picture a cookie looking up at the very stamper that made it and going, wait, have we MET? And it goes further: He came to His own, and His own did not receive Him.

cards.question: But to all who did receive the true Light and believed in His name, He gave the right to become ___ of God.
The children of God are born of blood or the will of man.

cards.text: They're born of God, friend. And now comes the line this whole song has been building to: "The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us."

cards.question: The Word became flesh, and we have seen His glory. Whose glory is it?

answers.text: The one and only Son from the Father
The great prophet sent from the Father
The mighty angel sent from the Father

cards.text: And He's full of grace and truth. Then John the Baptist cries out that the one who comes after him has surpassed him.

cards.question: John the Baptist says the one who comes after him has surpassed him because He was before him.

cards.text: From His fullness we have all received grace upon grace. That's like an oven where one batch comes out and the next one is ALREADY right behind it, all day, every day.

cards.question: The law was given through Moses, Israel's leader. Grace and truth came through ___.
No one has ever seen God. So who has made Him known?

cards.text: The Son, who is Himself God and is at the Father's side. That's how this song ends, friend: the Word who was with God in the beginning has made Him known.

findings.problem: The opening card explains what is happening but does not identify who is speaking or writing the Gospel, nor its audience. Addressing the baker as "Friend" does not supply that passage context.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The wrong answers "most" and "some" are not false when the right answer is "all." If all things were made through the Word, then most things and some things were also made through Him, so a baker could argue that either answer is true.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The retelling changes verse 10's concessive wording, "though the world was made through Him," into the simple statement "and the world was made through Him." This drops the contrast carried by "though."
The card cites only John 1:18, but its closing sentence also retells John 1:1-2 by describing "the Word who was with God in the beginning." The citation does not cover everything the card tells.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
